title: The path P_9 is an IR-graph: a nine-vertex counterexample to the Mynhardt-Roux non-IR conjecture for paths
beyond_target: accepted after the campaign target of 40 was reached (additional result #48 toward 60)
exact_endpoint: IR350452.conjecture_false : ¬ IR350452.Conjecture, where Conjecture := (forall n >= 3, ¬ IsIRGraph (pathGraph n)) ∧ (forall n >= 5, ¬ IsIRGraph (cycleGraph n)), IsIRGraph H := there are a finite vertex type V and G : SimpleGraph V with H ≃g IRGraph G, IRGraph G has the IR(G)-sets (irredundant sets of maximum cardinality, private neighbours via closed neighbourhoods) as vertices and the swap adjacency D' = insert v (D.erase u) with uv in E(G); witnessed by an explicit isomorphism pathGraph 9 ≃g IRGraph G9
scope: part (i) of the conjecture (paths) is false: P_9 is an IR-graph; computationally 9 is the minimum order of a graph whose IR-graph is a path of order >= 3 and P_7, P_8, P_9 occur at order 9; part (ii) (cycles) and P_6 remain open

Mynhardt-Roux, Irredundance Trees of Diameter 3, arXiv:2104.09004 (Discrete Math. 2022), Open Problems Conjecture 1

substantive_reason: It refutes a published conjecture on which graphs are IR-graphs (reconfiguration graphs of maximum irredundant sets), which the authors supported by proofs for P_3, P_4, P_5, C_5, C_6, C_7, with an explicit nine-vertex graph whose IR-graph is P_9, proved by a short hand-checkable argument and kernel-checked; exhaustive search shows nine vertices are needed. The graph is not a modification of any printed construction and does not follow from the source lemmas.
